summary: The preferred lean, low-allocation IObservable foundation for ReactiveUI 24+, with explicit System.Reactive-compatible package variants.
recommendedPatterns: Choose ReactiveUI.Primitives for new application and library pipelines.
Choose ReactiveUI.Primitives.Reactive only when full System.Reactive Unit, IScheduler, Subject, namespace, or public API compatibility is required.
Keep a pipeline in one reactive model and convert only at explicit package or application boundaries.
avoidPatterns: Do not add System.Reactive to a lean Primitives project solely for operators, scheduling, Unit, subjects, or disposables.
Do not reference removed ReactiveUI.Primitives.Extensions packages; those namespaces now ship from the base packages.
Do not mix ReactiveUI.Primitives and System.Reactive LINQ imports in the same file when shared operator names would be ambiguous.
setupSteps: Add ReactiveUI.Primitives for the default synchronous IObservable surface.
Add ReactiveUI.Primitives.Async only for IObservableAsync pipelines and a matching UI package only for the target framework.
Add ReactiveUI.Primitives.R3Bridge.Generator only when a consuming project needs generated R3 or R3Async boundary adapters.
commonPitfalls: The lean surface uses RxVoid and ISequencer instead of System.Reactive Unit and IScheduler.
The .Reactive packages intentionally retain a System.Reactive dependency and are not source-generator bridges.
R3 bridge generation requires the external R3 or R3Async symbols to be referenced by the consuming compilation.

features: BCL IObservable/IObserver pipelines without a System.Reactive runtime dependency
Low-allocation signals, sinks, state, commands, scheduling, virtual time, and disposables
WPF, WinForms, WinUI, Blazor, Avalonia, MAUI, Android, and Apple sequencing adapters
System.Reactive-compatible recompilations and optional generated R3/R3Async bridges
functions: Map/Select, Keep/Where, Fold/Scan, Reduce/Aggregate, Blend/Merge, Chain/Concat, Race/Amb, SwitchTo/Switch, Pair/Zip, SyncLatest/CombineLatest, Latch/WithLatestFrom, FlatMap/SelectMany
StateSignal, BehaviorSignal, ReplaySignal, FinalSignal, ConnectableSignal, ScheduledSignal, DelayableSignal, CommandSignal, TaskSignal
ImmediateSequencer, CurrentThreadSequencer, ThreadPoolSequencer, TaskPoolSequencer, SynchronizationContextSequencer, VirtualClock
Disposable.Create, MultipleDisposable/CompositeDisposable, Pocket, Slot, AssignmentSlot, CancellationDisposable, DisposeWith
options: Lean RxVoid/ISequencer or .Reactive Unit/IScheduler package family
Matching lean or .Reactive UI sequencer package
Optional standalone R3 bridge analyzer with no runtime R3 dependency
packageSelection: Default: ReactiveUI.Primitives; disposables-only: ReactiveUI.Disposables; low-level composition: ReactiveUI.Primitives.Core
Full System.Reactive compatibility: ReactiveUI.Primitives.Reactive and, when needed, ReactiveUI.Primitives.Async.Reactive
UI: ReactiveUI.Primitives.Wpf, WinForms, WinUI, Blazor, Avalonia, or Maui; append .Reactive only for full Rx compatibility
sourceGeneratorGuidance: Source generators are not needed for core IObservable operators.
Prefer the R3Bridge generator over handwritten R3/R3Async adapters when the supported external symbols are present.
compatibilityNotes: ReactiveUI.Primitives.Reactive recompiles the same engine against System.Reactive Unit and IScheduler.
Extension-helper namespaces remain available from ReactiveUI.Primitives and ReactiveUI.Primitives.Reactive after the old Extensions packages were folded in.
Mixed System.Reactive.Linq and ReactiveUI.Primitives imports can make shared names ambiguous; use Map/Keep or complete the file migration.
migrationGuidance: Map Unit to RxVoid, IScheduler to ISequencer, Subject<T> to Signal<T>, BehaviorSubject<T> to BehaviorSignal<T>/StateSignal<T>, and ReplaySubject<T> to ReplaySignal<T>.
Map Observable factories to Signal factories and CompositeDisposable/SerialDisposable to MultipleDisposable/Slot equivalents.
Preserve Rx operator aliases initially, then adopt Primitives names incrementally; remove System.Reactive only after public API and imports are clean.
If binary/source compatibility must be preserved, move that surface to a .Reactive boundary rather than mixing lean types internally.
